Power Rankings · Week 1

  1. 1

    Colorado Avalanche

    2-0-0Record2.00PTS/GP+9Goal diff2-0-0Last 10+750Cup odds

    2-0 with a +9, after 8-4 over the Kings and 6-1 over the Blues, and O'Connor and L'Heureux look set to return this week. Last season's best team just took the top spot from the champs.

  2. 2

    Carolina Hurricanes

    2-1-1Record1.25PTS/GP-1Goal diff2-1-1Last 10+700Cup odds

    1-1-1 and -3: a 1-0 extra-time loss to Florida, a 5-2 home loss to Washington, then an OT win in Philly. A slow week, but one week doesn't undo a Cup.

  3. 3

    Minnesota Wild

    2-0-1Record1.67PTS/GP+4Goal diff2-0-1Last 10+1300Cup odds

    2-0 and +5, beating Nashville 3-1 and Boston 4-1. Even without Gustavsson, the goaltending has given up one goal a night.

  4. 4

Wednesday, October 7

Game recap

NSH4TOR5OTFinal: NSH 4, TOR 5 OT

Nashville built a 3-0 lead in Toronto and then handed it back one goal at a time, like a gambler who doesn't know when to leave the table. Steven Stamkos scored on the power play, Nils Hoglander scored twice, and it was 3-0 just 3:03 into the second. Then the Leafs woke up: John Tavares (with an assist from Anthony Stolarz, of all people), William Nylander on the power play, and after Stamkos made it 4-2, Gavin McKenna scored his first NHL goal. Jack Roslovic tied it 8:54 into the third, and Auston Matthews ended it 4:46 into overtime from Nylander, finishing with a goal and three assists. Toronto outshot Nashville 37-25. Juuse Saros made 32 saves; Stolarz made 21. The Leafs are 2-2. Nashville, 1-1-1, led by three on the road and left with one point, which is the most Predators way to spend a Tuesday.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR6MTL4Final: CAR 6, MTL 4

Montreal threw a home-opener party and the team that ended its season last spring showed up uninvited and ate all the food. The first period had five goals and no defense: Taylor Hall scored 2:25 in, Zachary Bolduc and Nick Suzuki answered inside two minutes, and Bolduc's power-play goal made it 3-2 Habs after one. Then Carolina took over. Sebastian Aho tied it on the power play, Mark Jankowski put the Canes ahead, and Hall's second made it 5-3 with eight minutes left. Juraj Slafkovsky got one back with the goalie pulled, and Andrei Svechnikov hit the empty net. Aho finished with a goal and two assists. Brandon Bussi, a surprise starter, won with 16 saves on 20; Jakub Dobes stopped 28 of 33. Carolina outshot Montreal 34-20. The Canadiens are 1-1-1 and have now allowed 12 goals in two games, which is a lot of pucks for one Bell Centre to watch go in.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT3DET5Final: OTT 3, DET 5

Dylan Larkin asked to be traded this summer, lost the C, got booed at the opener, and then walked into his season debut and gave Detroit its first win. Hockey is a funny business. Tim Stützle opened it 2:44 in, Alex DeBrincat tied it 32 seconds later, and Larkin put the Wings ahead late in the first. Viktor Arvidsson scored on the power play and Justin Faulk made it 4-1 by 4:30 of the second. Drake Batherson and William Eklund pulled Ottawa within one, but DeBrincat finished it with a power-play empty-netter at 19:10 for his second of the night. Lucas Raymond had three assists, Larkin a goal and an assist, and rookie William Wallinder picked up a point in his NHL debut. John Gibson made 22 saves; Samuel Ersson made 31 on 35. Detroit is 1-2. Ottawa's perfect start lasted exactly two games, which is about one more than Senators fans had budgeted for.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA5NJD3Final: UTA 5, NJD 3

Utah scored twice on the power play, and the Devils' defense went missing for the rest of it. Clayton Keller scored on the power play 1:57 in, Luke Evangelista answered on New Jersey's, and the teams traded goals until Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal (his fifth already) and Lawson Crouse's at 19:03 of the second made it 4-2. Jesper Boqvist got the Devils within one in the third, and Vincent Trocheck, playing through a lower-body injury, scored his first goal as a Mammoth to close it. Schmaltz had a goal and two assists, Mikhail Sergachev three assists. Evangelista scored both New Jersey goals, and Timo Meier fired eight shots for one assist. Brenden Dillon and Jack McBain fought in the third. Karel Vejmelka made 30 saves; Jake Allen stopped 26 of 31. Utah is 3-1. The Devils are 1-2 and minus-7, and the blue line is starting to look like a waiting room.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN2BUF3OTFinal: MIN 2, BUF 3 OT

Minnesota led 2-0 with 25 minutes left and then remembered it was in Buffalo, where nice leads go to die. Danila Yurov scored on the power play at 13:53 of the second and Maxim Shabanov added another 1:45 later. Noah Ostlund cut it in half early in the third, Tage Thompson tied it at 9:38 on a night he reached 400 points as a Sabre, and Owen Power won it 4:22 into overtime from Jiri Kulich and Thompson. Thompson fired nine shots, Power and Thompson each had a goal and an assist, and Colten Ellis won his first start with 18 saves on 20. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 25 of 28. Matt Boldy had seven shots and nothing to show for them, and Kirill Kaprizov went pointless in 25 minutes. The Sabres are 2-1. The Wild got a point, which is nice, but they also blew a two-goal third-period lead to Buffalo, which is the kind of thing a team should keep out of the group chat.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI2NYR5Final: NYI 2, NYR 5

Alexis Lafrenière got a hat trick, and two-thirds of it was delivered to an empty net 32 seconds apart. Nobody at MSG asked for a receipt. Oliver Bjorkstrand opened the scoring and Lafrenière made it 2-0 25 seconds into the second, but the Islanders tied it within five minutes on goals from Bo Horvat (power play) and Calum Ritchie. Bjorkstrand's power-play goal at 17:07 of the second was the winner, his second of the night and his first two as a Ranger. Lafrenière then scored at 18:22 and 18:54 of the third with Semyon Varlamov on the bench. He also had an assist. There were two fights: Brayden Schenn and J.T. Miller in the first, Bjorkstrand and Adam Pelech in the final seconds. Varlamov, in his first NHL game since November 2024, made 19 saves; Igor Shesterkin made 17. The Rangers have won four straight. The Islanders are 1-2 and lost the Battle of New York on a pair of empty nets.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL2CHI4Final: STL 2, CHI 4

Chicago finally won a hockey game, and it picked the home opener to do it, which is good showmanship from a team that hadn't shown much else. Mason McTavish gave St. Louis the lead late in the first. In the second, Sam Rinzel tied it on the power play and Anton Frondell put the Hawks ahead two minutes later. The last 69 seconds were a fire drill: Cole Smith scored shorthanded into the empty net, Connor McMichael answered on the power play with Hofer pulled, and Frank Nazar hit the empty net again with four seconds left. Nazar and Frondell each had a goal and an assist. Spencer Knight made 26 saves on 28; Joel Hofer stopped 17 of 19. Colton Parayko tied Barret Jackman for the most games by a Blues defenseman. St. Louis is 1-2 to close its opening road trip and just gave a 1-3 rebuild its first win of the year. That's charity, not hockey.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK6SEA2Final: VGK 6, SEA 2

Vegas went to Seattle and treated the Kraken like a comp'd buffet. It was 5-0 before the second intermission: Victor Olofsson scored twice, Tomas Hertl on the power play, Mark Stone shorthanded, and Jack Eichel unassisted with 31 seconds left in the period. Hertl added another power-play goal in the third. Hertl (two goals, two assists) and Eichel (a goal, three assists) had four points each. Joey Daccord was pulled after allowing five on 21 shots; Philipp Grubauer stopped 6 of 7. Shane Wright and Jared McCann scored for Seattle. It got nasty late: Brandon Montour fought Stone and took 17 penalty minutes, Marc Gatcomb fought Ryan Winterton, and Ben Meyers was thrown out for boarding Olofsson, with a league hearing expected. Carter Hart made 25 saves. Vegas is 3-1. Seattle is 2-2, and the Kraken's best work of the night came after the game was already gone.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA2LAK1Final: FLA 2, LAK 1

The Panthers needed four games and a cross-country flight to win one in regulation, but they got it, 2-1 in the Kings' home opener. Alex Laferriere scored with a minute left in the first for Los Angeles. Seth Jones tied it 3:49 into the second, and Matthew Tkachuk won it at 11:20 of the third from Sam Bennett. Jacob Markstrom stopped 19 of 20, and the Kings managed just 20 shots in their own building. Darcy Kuemper made 26 saves on 28 and deserved better. Garnet Hathaway and Joel Edmundson fought in the second. Artemi Panarin had four shots and no points. Florida is 2-0-2. Los Angeles is 0-2-1, one of two teams in the West still without a win, and its home crowd paid opening-night prices to watch 20 shots in 60 minutes.

Tuesday, October 6

Game recap

PHI1TBL4Final: PHI 1, TBL 4

The Flyers finally got a goaltender to keep them in a game and then forgot the part where you shoot the puck. Philadelphia managed 14 shots all night, Tampa Bay put up 36, and the Lightning won 4-1. Brayden Point opened it late in the first from John Carlson and Nikita Kucherov, and Pontus Holmberg made it 2-0 just 17 seconds into the second. Tyson Foerster got one back, then Ilya Mikheyev restored the cushion with three minutes left and Brandon Hagel, who fired eight shots, hit the empty net with seven seconds to go. Kucherov had two assists, Holmberg and Mikheyev a goal and an assist each. Dan Vladar made 32 saves on 35 and deserved a better team in front of him. Andrei Vasilevskiy needed 13 saves for his 372nd career win, tying Andy Moog for 20th all-time.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT4BOS1Final: OTT 4, BOS 1

Ottawa walked into TD Garden and acted like it held the lease. Tim Stützle scored shorthanded at 7:39 of the first and again 1:43 later, set up Drake Batherson 66 seconds into the second, and finished with three points and career goal number 150, the fourth German-born player to get there. Michael Amadio made it 4-0 at 5:19 of the second. Linus Ullmark stopped all 10 shots he saw and came out after two periods following a crease collision with JJ Peterka; Samuel Ersson stopped 8 of 9 in relief, and the one was James Hagens early in the third. Jeremy Swayman made 20 saves on 24. The final seconds brought misconducts for Nikita Zadorov, Tanner Jeannot and Nick Cousins, the most physical Boston got all night. The Senators are 2-0. The Bruins have lost two straight, and their power play (0-for-4) is still looking for the arena.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG3PIT2Final: WPG 3, PIT 2

Two goalies making their season debuts traded saves for 40 minutes, and then the third period turned into a pinball machine. Ben Kindel gave Pittsburgh the lead at 9:27 of the second from Declan Carlile and Erik Karlsson. Alex Iafallo tied it 4:43 into the third, and Adam Lowry put Winnipeg ahead at 7:08 with Iafallo and Dylan DeMelo on the helpers. Carlile answered at 8:53 to make it 2-2, and the Penguins enjoyed that tie for exactly nine seconds before Cole Perfetti scored the winner from Josh Morrissey. Clay Stevenson made 30 saves on 32 in his Jets debut; Sergei Murashov stopped 31 of 34. Sidney Crosby had five shots and no points, Kyle Connor six shots and no points. The Jets are 2-0-1. Pittsburgh's lead lasted a period, its tie lasted nine seconds, and its defensive coverage on the winner lasted even less.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS0DAL5Final: SJS 0, DAL 5

Dallas came in 0-2 and needed a soft landing. San Jose, without Macklin Celebrini after he was scratched late, provided the pillow. Miro Heiskanen opened it at 18:51 of the first from Roope Hintz and Jamie Benn, and the second period settled it: Joel Kiviranta at 3:17, Benn at 6:19, Jason Robertson at 16:30. Mikko Rantanen added the fifth midway through the third. Hintz had two assists, Benn and Robertson a goal and an assist each. Jake Oettinger needed only 13 saves for the shutout, the kind of night where the hardest part of the job is staying awake. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 21 of 26 and spent most of it on an island. The Stars outshot the Sharks 26-13 and got their first win. Thirteen shots in 60 minutes: the Sharks have been rebuilding for years and still haven't installed a forecheck.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, October 5

Game recap

WPG3DET2Final: WPG 3, DET 2

Detroit kept taking penalties and Winnipeg kept saying thank you. Cole Perfetti scored on the power play at 13:04 of the first, Kyle Connor did it again 92 seconds later, and Connor's second, 5:41 into the second, made it 3-0. Three power-play goals, all of them with Perfetti and Josh Morrissey's fingerprints on them: Connor finished with two goals and an assist, Perfetti a goal and two helpers, Morrissey two assists and seven shots. Viktor Arvidsson got one back on a Wings power play late in the second and Emmitt Finnie made it 3-2 early in the third, and then Stuart Skinner closed the door: 33 saves on 35. John Gibson stopped 24 of 27. Tyrel Bauer and Keegan Kolesar fought in the first, the only part of the afternoon Detroit won on points. The Jets are 1-0-1. The Red Wings are 0-2, the fans are chanting at ownership again, and "Hockeytown" is starting to read like false advertising.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA2NYR4Final: UTA 2, NYR 4

Vincent Trocheck came back to the Garden and left with two shots, no points and a loss. Vladislav Gavrikov opened it late in the first from Adam Fox, Nick Schmaltz tied it on a Utah power play in the second (his fourth already), and then the Rangers took the third. Gabe Perreault scored 3:15 in from Alexis Lafrenière and Mika Zibanejad, J.T. Miller made it 3-1 from Gavrikov, who finished with a goal and an assist. Andrew Peeke cut it to 3-2 with five minutes left, and Eeli Tolvanen hit the empty net, with Igor Shesterkin picking up the assist: one game after scoring a goal, the man is now a playmaker too. He stopped 28 of 30 between points. Karel Vejmelka made 18 saves on 21. Will Cuylle and Jack McBain fought early in the third. The Rangers have won three straight. Utah is 2-1, and mammoths have a long history of things going badly once the ice shows up.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA2ANA3OTFinal: FLA 2, ANA 3 OT

Brad Marchand came off IR weeks ahead of schedule, tied the game with the goalie pulled, and Florida still lost. Cutter Gauthier scored on the power play late in the first, Carter Verhaeghe answered 51 seconds later, and Gauthier struck on another power play 47 seconds into the second. The Ducks held 2-1 until 18:10 of the third, when Marchand, from Lars Eller, tied it 6-on-5 in his season debut. Then Florida went to the box in overtime, and Mikael Granlund won it on the power play at 4:14, from Leo Carlsson and Gauthier. Gauthier finished with two goals and an assist; Carlsson had three assists, which helps explain the offer sheet. Lukas Dostal stopped 29 of 31, Jacob Markstrom 18 of 21. Anaheim is 2-0. Florida is 1-0-2 with three straight overtime games, and three Ducks power-play goals say the two-time champs think the penalty box is a spa.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1SEA6Final: CGY 1, SEA 6

Seattle's home opener was over before the popcorn got cold. Berkly Catton scored unassisted 2:22 in, Mackie Samoskevich made it 2-0 at 4:40, and Bobby McMann made it 3-0 at 7:40. Shane Wright added one in the second from Catton, and Samoskevich scored again with 26 seconds left in the period, a fine first night on his new line. Morgan Frost broke the shutout on a third-period power play, and Jordan Eberle restored the five-goal lead 39 seconds later, just to be rude about it. Brandon Montour and Chandler Stephenson had two assists each, and Catton finished with a goal and an assist. Joey Daccord stopped 32 of 33; Dustin Wolf stopped 21 of 27 and gave up six to Seattle for the second time in four days. Calgary is 0-3 and minus-13, and has lost five straight to Seattle by a combined 25-6. The Flames aren't a rival anymore; they're the Kraken's favorite home-opener party favor.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK3VAN2Final: VGK 3, VAN 2

Vancouver scored first, and Vegas spent the rest of the night reminding the Canucks who owns this matchup. Paul Cotter put Vancouver up on the power play late in the first, his fourth already. Then the Golden Knights took the second: Mitch Marner tied it 9:01 in, Victor Olofsson scored on the power play from Mark Stone and Jack Eichel, Jonathan Lekkerimäki tied it 2-2 at 17:54, and 34 seconds later Marc Gatcomb, from Braeden Bowman and Nic Dowd, put Vegas back ahead for good. Nobody scored in the third. Adin Hill got the start and stopped 18 of 20, mostly because Vancouver managed only 20 shots. Kevin Lankinen made 25 saves on 28. Vegas is 2-1. The Canucks are 2-2 on the second night of a back-to-back, and losing to the Golden Knights is still the one tradition in Vancouver nobody had to rebuild.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, October 4

Game recap

CHI3BUF4Final: CHI 3, BUF 4

Chicago did the hard part. Ryan Donato and Tyler Bertuzzi had the Hawks up 2-0 in the first, Oliver Moore put them back ahead 3-2 late in the second, and Anton Frondell set up two of the three. Then the third period happened, as it tends to in Chicago. Rasmus Dahlin tied it 6:10 in and Jiri Kulich buried the winner at 13:20, with Tage Thompson (goal, assist) and Jack Quinn also scoring for Buffalo. The Hawks managed 15 shots all night, so Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 12 and mostly enjoyed the view; Spencer Knight made 24 saves on 28 and deserved better company. Buffalo native Patrick Kane went home and left with zero points and a minor. Chicago is 0-3 and minus-10: the rebuild is still under construction, and the third period is a load-bearing wall made of cardboard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT3TOR2Final: OTT 3, TOR 2

Ottawa opened its season by beating Toronto in Toronto, which remains the Senators' favorite way to spend a Saturday. Thomas Chabot scored late in the first, Auston Matthews answered 33 seconds into the second, and Kirill Marchenko gave the Leafs a 2-1 lead on the power play. Toronto held it for five and a half minutes. Michael Amadio tied it from Tim Stützle and Chabot, and Stephen Halliday won it 9:46 into the third off feeds from Fabian Zetterlund and Claude Giroux. Shots finished 29 apiece; Linus Ullmark stopped 27, Sergei Bobrovsky 26, and the difference was who blinked in the third. The Leafs blinked. Toronto is 1-2 with a new coach and a new goalie, and the same old feeling of watching a lead walk out the door with the Senators holding it open.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH1TBL3Final: WSH 1, TBL 3

Tampa Bay's 11-forward, seven-defenseman experiment paid off in every way it could. Charle-Edouard D'Astous scored 2:26 in, Conor Geekie made it 2-0 late in the first (Brandon Hagel and Jake Guentzel set up both), and the extra defenseman, Emil Lilleberg, found time to fight Vincent Desharnais in the second. Justin Sourdif got Washington on the board 7:04 into the second, and that was the whole Capitals offense: Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 of 21. Charlie Lindgren was sharp at the other end (27 of 29) and it didn't matter. Guentzel finished it with an empty-netter for a goal and two assists, and the Lightning have their first win. Washington spent the summer buying forwards and came home with 21 shots: all that shopping, nothing in the bag.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR3PHI2OTFinal: CAR 3, PHI 2 OT

Shayne Gostisbehere came back to Philadelphia and scored a big power-play goal, just like old times, only for the other team. Sebastian Aho scored 10 seconds into the game, Owen Tippett and Matvei Michkov turned it into a 2-1 Flyers lead, and Aho tied it on the power play 4:59 into the third. Then Gostisbehere ended it on another power play at 2:51 of overtime, from Jackson Blake and Aho. Joseph Woll was the only reason it got that far: 37 saves on 40 as Carolina outshot Philly 40-18. Pyotr Kochetkov needed just 16 saves. The Flyers are 0-1-2, the hockey version of showing up to every party and leaving before the cake: three games, two points, minus-9, and an old friend delivering the bad news in their own building.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL5PIT6OTFinal: MTL 5, PIT 6 OT

Pittsburgh built a 5-1 lead by the middle of the second period, then spent the next 25 minutes handing it back like an overdue library book. Evgeni Malkin (goal, two assists), Declan Carlile, Samuel Girard, Tommy Novak and Ben Kindel did the building. Nick Suzuki started the demolition late in the second, Cole Caufield scored his second of the night early in the third, and with Jakub Dobes pulled Montreal scored twice in 24 seconds: Chris Kreider at 18:52 and Ivan Demidov at 19:16. Suzuki finished with a goal and three assists, Lane Hutson with three helpers. Then Novak, from Malkin and Kris Letang, won it 1:33 into overtime for his second of the night. Both goalies stopped exactly 80 percent. The Penguins are 2-0. Montreal got a point and a lesson: comebacks are fun, but spotting a team four goals is how you end up with a Cup drought old enough to have a mortgage.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA4CBJ1Final: UTA 4, CBJ 1

Utah walked into Columbus and won it on special teams. Mikhail Sergachev opened the scoring on the power play, Nick Schmaltz made it 2-0 before the first intermission, and after Kent Johnson (from Matthew Knies) cut it to 2-1 early in the second, the Utah power play struck twice more in the third: Dylan Guenther, then Schmaltz again. Three power-play goals, two goals for Schmaltz (three on the season) and a goal and two assists for Guenther (three goals in two games). Clayton Keller and Logan Cooley had two assists apiece. Sebastian Cossa stopped 17 of 18, because 18 was all Columbus could find; Jet Greaves made 27 saves on 31. Utah is 2-0 and plus-9 and heads to Madison Square Garden tonight. The Blue Jackets kept handing Utah power plays and shot like a team that left its sticks on the bus.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA1EDM3Final: SEA 1, EDM 3

Edmonton's two best players waited until the last three minutes and then clocked in. Owen Michaels scored 2:51 into the game for his second of the season, Bobby McMann tied it on a Seattle power play in the second, and it sat at 1-1 until Leon Draisaitl, from Connor McDavid, scored with 2:27 left. McDavid added the empty-netter 82 seconds later, because of course he did. Devon Levi stopped 19 of 20; Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 24 and kept Seattle alive for 57 minutes. Ryan Lindgren and Trent Frederic dropped the gloves in the first period, the most physical thing the Kraken attack did all night. Seattle is 1-1 and comes home to face Calgary tonight with 20 shots of evidence that its offense is still exploring the ocean floor.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD0NYI6Final: NJD 0, NYI 6

Ilya Sorokin made 37 saves, and New Jersey spent the night finding out what a brick wall feels like. The Devils outshot the Islanders 37-32 and lost 6-0, which takes real talent. Simon Holmstrom and Brayden Schenn scored 88 seconds apart early in the second, Bo Horvat added a power-play goal, and the third turned into a group project: Victor Eklund, Ondrej Palat and Casey Cizikas, the last one shorthanded with 1:19 left. Six goals, six different scorers. Matthew Schaefer had two assists and Eklund a goal and an assist. Nico Daws stopped 26 of 32 and got no help from anybody. The Islanders even up at 1-1. The Devils are minus-5 two games in, and their offense got lost somewhere on the Long Island Expressway and still hasn't called home.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL1NSH2Final: DAL 1, NSH 2

Miro Heiskanen scored 47 seconds in, and Dallas apparently decided that was enough work for the second half of a back-to-back. Nashville answered with two power-play goals in the first period: Steven Stamkos, from Ryan O'Reilly and Roman Josi, and Nils Hoglander, his first as a Predator, from Jack Ahcan and Alexander Kerfoot. Then nobody scored for the last 44 minutes. Juuse Saros stopped 29 of 30; Casey DeSmith made 24 saves on 26 and was fine. Waiver pickup William Trudeau played his first NHL game, and Ahcan picked up a point in his Predators debut. The Stars are 0-2 and minus-5, and a team that piled up 112 points last season is now giving away power-play goals like free samples at the grocery store.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS1MIN4Final: BOS 1, MIN 4

Tanner Jeannot scored 1:53 in for Boston, and the Bruins spent the next 58 minutes learning why you don't hand Minnesota power plays. Kirill Kaprizov tied it on the power play in the second, Quinn Hughes put the Wild ahead on another one six minutes later, Jared Spurgeon made it 3-1 early in the third, and Kaprizov closed it with an unassisted empty-netter. That's three goals in two games for Kaprizov; Hughes added an assist to his goal. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 26 of 27, and the Wild are 2-0. Michael DiPietro made 26 saves on 29 for Boston. The Bruins fall to 2-1, which is fine, but their offense after the first two minutes was a Boston traffic jam: plenty of horn, no movement.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL1COL6Final: STL 1, COL 6

Colorado scored the first six goals, and St. Louis spent the night looking for the exit. Cale Makar opened it 4:09 in, Martin Necas added another in the first, and the second period was a highlight reel: Josh Manson, Artturi Lehkonen (unassisted, already his third), Nicolas Roy, and Necas again, the last two 23 seconds apart late in the period. Necas finished with two goals and an assist; Nathan MacKinnon had three assists without scoring, which is how he relaxes. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 of 26 and lost the shutout to Dalibor Dvorsky early in the third. Jordan Binnington faced 36 shots and wore six of them. Colorado is 2-0 and plus-9. The Blues brought their new, younger look to Denver and found out the altitude isn't the only thing there that leaves you gasping.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1VAN4Final: CGY 1, VAN 4

For 40 minutes Calgary had a lead, a fight and a plan. Luke Schenn and Adam Klapka went at it 2:55 in, Matt Coronato scored on the power play late in the first, and Devin Cooley carried a 1-0 lead into the third. Then Vancouver scored four times in the final 20. Liam Ohgren tied it 88 seconds in, Elias Pettersson put the Canucks ahead from Ohgren and Tom Willander, Drew O'Connor added one with 3:27 left, and Aatu Räty hit the empty net. Linus Karlsson and Willander had two assists each. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 23 of 24; Cooley made 22 saves on 25. The Flames are 0-2 and minus-8 and play in Seattle tonight on the back end of a back-to-back, after blowing a third-period lead to the team that finished last in the league a year ago. Flames fans will be hearing that sentence in their sleep.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK4SJS5OTFinal: LAK 4, SJS 5 OT

San Jose and Los Angeles played 63 minutes of hockey that needed a scorekeeper on overtime pay. Adrian Kempe opened it on the power play, then the Sharks scored three straight: Tyler Toffoli on a power play, Kiefer Sherwood unassisted, and Nolan Allan. Quinton Byfield answered on the power play with two seconds left in the second, Igor Chernyshov made it 4-2, and the Kings tied it with goals from Erik Haula and Artemi Panarin, the second at the 15-minute mark of the third. Then Macklin Celebrini found Chernyshov 3:18 into overtime for his second of the night. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 31 of 35, Anton Forsberg 20 of 25. San Jose is 2-0. The Kings outshot the Sharks 35-25 and still lost, a very Kings way to spend a Saturday: all the puck, none of the points, one point in two games.

Saturday, October 3

Game recap

NYR2DET0Final: NYR 2, DET 0

Detroit's home opener had everything a long-suffering fan base could want: booing their own former captain before puck drop, then 60 minutes of not scoring. Dylan Garand, the Rangers' fill-in on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped all 22 shots for the shutout, which is what happens when the other team's shots arrive gift-wrapped. Sean Durzi scored on the power play 5:12 in and later fought Marco Kasper, a full night's work before the third period. Eeli Tolvanen hit the empty net with 1:16 left. John Gibson made 19 saves on 20 and got nothing for it but a sympathetic slap on the pads. New York is 2-1 and has won two straight. Detroit is 0-1, has no goals, no captain and a 10-season playoff drought, and the season is one game old.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH5CAR2Final: WSH 5, CAR 2

The Capitals walked into the champs' building and had it 3-0 before the first intermission, the hockey version of showing up to a party and eating the cake. Alex Tuch scored twice in his Washington debut, and rookie defenseman Cole Hutson scored in his NHL debut, which beats the usual first-game souvenir of a puck and a nervous smile. Ovechkin got an assist on the opening goal, Jakob Chychrun had a power-play goal and an assist, and Dylan Strome and Pierre-Luc Dubois had two helpers each. Sebastian Aho finally got Carolina a power-play goal in the second, and Ryan Leonard answered eight seconds later, which is just rude. Logan Thompson made 31 saves on 33; Brandon Bussi let in five on 27. The Hurricanes outshot Washington and lost by three: 0-1-1, one goal in two home games, and the banner is already the best thing they've put up this season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS4WPG3OTFinal: BOS 4, WPG 3 OT

Winnipeg's home opener was a lovely evening right up until the last 1:38. The Jets led 3-2 after Mario Ferraro scored with eight seconds left in the second, Kyle Connor had a power-play goal, an assist and nine shots, and the Canada Life Centre was ready to go home happy. Then Boston pulled Jeremy Swayman, and Elias Lindholm tied it 6-on-5 at 18:22 of the third. JJ Peterka, two games into his Bruins career, won it 3:21 into overtime for his second goal. David Pastrnak and Nikita Zadorov set up two goals each, Hampus Lindholm and James Hagens also scored, and Mark Kastelic and Tyrel Bauer dropped the gloves early. Swayman stopped 30 of 33, Stuart Skinner 26 of 30. Boston is 2-0. Winnipeg got a point for its trouble, and a reminder that its former Vezina winner is still suspended for skipping camp and still waiting on a trade. Nothing says 'new season' like the old goalie problem.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL4DAL0Final: STL 4, DAL 0

Dallas spent the summer near the top of everybody's rankings and opened its season by getting shut out at home. Mason McTavish, playing his first game as a Blue, scored 94 seconds in, and the Stars spent the next 58 minutes looking for a reply. Dalibor Dvorsky made it 2-0 in the second, then St. Louis hit the empty net twice in 15 seconds, Jimmy Snuggerud and Pius Suter, with Joel Hofer picking up an assist on the second one. Hofer stopped all 25 shots for the shutout and outscored the entire Dallas roster in points. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves on 22 and deserved a better band in front of him. Jake Neighbours and Arttu Hyry fought in the second, the closest Dallas came to winning a battle all night. A 112-point team with Jason Robertson locked up, and the first goal of their season will have to wait for Nashville.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA4VGK3Final: ANA 4, VGK 3

Anaheim's season opener in Vegas went great for about 45 minutes and then got very Vegas. Beckett Sennecke scored with eight seconds left in the first, Alex Killorn and Jeff Malott scored 55 seconds apart early in the second, and Leo Carlsson, the guy the Ducks paid to keep away from Philadelphia, made it 4-0 at 7:03. The Golden Knights trailed by four on home ice to a team that just lost half its summer roster, and the Strip briefly considered a dinner show. Then Shea Theodore, Tomas Hertl on the power play and Braeden Bowman with 2:50 left made it 4-3, and Jack Eichel had two assists in the rally. Lukas Dostal held on with 27 saves on 30. Carter Hart let in four on 20. Vegas played the last 20 minutes like Cup finalists and the first 40 like the house was comping the other team.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Friday, October 2

Game recap

PHI2NJD3OTFinal: PHI 2, NJD 3 OT

The Devils threw 44 shots at Joseph Woll, the hockey version of trying every key on the ring. Woll stopped 41 and dragged Philly to overtime, where Jack Hughes ended it at 3:23, because of course he did. The Flyers led twice: once on a Rasmus Ristolainen goal with their own goalie on the bench (bold), once on Travis Sanheim's goal early in the third. Both leads lasted about as long as a Philly sports-radio caller's patience. Dougie Hamilton and Luke Hughes did the tying, Bratt set up the winner, and Jake Allen needed only 23 saves. Tocchet shortened his bench so much that Porter Martone watched most of the third from the best seat in the house. One point and a minus-8 goal difference after two games: the Flyers are rebuilding, and so far the foundation is Joseph Woll and a lot of prayer.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL1NYR5Final: TBL 1, NYR 5

Igor Shesterkin stopped 24 of 25 and then, apparently tired of waiting on his forwards, scored into the empty net himself. A goalie goal in the home opener: the Garden hasn't been this giddy since the last time somebody promised a parade. Zibanejad scored on the power play and set up another, Dorofeyev had two points, and Adam Fox handed out two assists like party favors. Tolvanen and Gabe Perreault joined in. Kucherov got one back in the second and then spent the night watching. Andrei Vasilevskiy let in four on 24 shots, not the opening act Tampa sold tickets for. Final tally: the entire Lightning roster scored one goal, exactly as many as the guy in the Rangers' crease, and he was busy making 24 saves at the time.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3CBJ6Final: BUF 3, CBJ 6

Matthew Knies' first game in a Blue Jackets sweater: two goals, an assist and, presumably, a thank-you card in the mail to Columbus. Charlie Coyle had three assists, Werenski two, and Columbus scored six on 23 shots, efficiency Buffalo can only read about. The Sabres hung around, 4-3 after two thanks to Quinn and Helenius, then remembered who they were. Luukkonen stopped 17 of 22, a save percentage best described as 'hospitable'. Mathieu Olivier fought Zach Metsa and then scored into the empty net, a full shift's work in one night. Owen Power and Noah Ostlund had two assists each, nice consolation prizes. Buffalo opened the season with 'this is the year' energy and closed the first night with 'here we go again.'

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN3NSH1Final: MIN 3, NSH 1

Nashville rolled out the home-opener pageantry and the Wild treated it like a soundcheck. Nick Foligno opened the scoring, Blake Coleman added a power-play goal, and Kaprizov put it away early in the third off a Quinn Hughes feed, a sentence Wild fans waited all summer to say. Hughes played 27:30 and looked like he'd been there for years. Jesper Wallstedt needed 19 saves, a light shift. Josi scored, Stamkos and Forsberg got assists, and the Preds managed 20 shots in their own building, roughly one per sad country song. Saros made 27 saves and deserved a better band behind him. Nashville spent big two summers ago to win now, and 'now' keeps showing up looking like this.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA6CGY1Final: SEA 6, CGY 1

Calgary's home opener was over about 19 and a half minutes in, when the Kraken went up 3-0 and the Saddledome started checking the parking-lot traffic. Vince Dunn had three points, Jared McCann three assists, and Joey Daccord stopped 24 of 25 and still found time for an assist, which is one more point than the Flames' entire defense managed. Seattle's scoresheet read like a roll call: Eberle, Dunn, Gaudreau, Stephenson, Beniers, Kakko. Dustin Wolf faced 32 shots and six went in, and very little of it was his idea. Ryan Strome broke the shutout with 3:25 left, which in Calgary currently counts as a rally. The Flames have a shiny new arena on the way, and on this evidence it'll open before their second goal of the night would have.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA3SJS4OTFinal: FLA 3, SJS 4 OT

The Sharks led Florida 3-0, which in San Jose is screenshot material. Will Smith scored shorthanded and on the power play in the same period, Celebrini set up three goals and put seven shots on net, and the building was ready to name a freeway after somebody. Then the Panthers woke up: Luostarinen twice and Matthew Tkachuk 17 seconds later, because Florida treats a three-goal hole like a mild inconvenience. Luca Cagnoni ended it in overtime anyway. Brady Tkachuk and Jacob Trouba dropped the gloves in the first, and Collin Graf and Uvis Balinskis followed suit in the second, so nobody left without a souvenir. Florida has Cup rings in the trophy case and just lost an overtime to a team that finished dead last in 2025: the champs' swagger made the trip, the finishing touch stayed in Sunrise.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI0UTA6Final: CHI 0, UTA 6

Utah's home opener was a 6-0 party, and the Blackhawks brought 15 shots to it, which isn't a gift so much as an IOU. Dylan Guenther scored twice on the power play, Keller had two assists, and six different Mammoth scored, including Anders Lee in his first home game for his new team. Karel Vejmelka made 15 saves for the shutout and probably had time to reorganize the bench. Arvid Soderblom got a surprise start and 32 shots for his trouble. Ryan Donato fought MacKenzie Weegar in the third, the most competitive thing Chicago did all night. Two games, 0-2, minus-9: Chicago keeps saying the rebuild is almost finished, and the contractor still can't find the net.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM9VAN7Final: EDM 9, VAN 7

Sixteen goals in Vancouver, which is what happens when two teams agree defense is a rumor. McDavid had five points, Draisaitl three, and the Oilers scored twice shorthanded in 34 seconds, which is just rude. It was 8-2 midway through the second and Kevin Lankinen's night was over. Then Edmonton did the most Oilers thing possible and let Vancouver score four straight, Marco Rossi twice, before Draisaitl calmed everybody down on the power play. Devon Levi gave up seven on 22 shots and still got the win, the hockey version of failing the exam and getting into the school anyway. Elias Pettersson had three points and eight hits, so at least one Canuck showed up angry. Vancouver had all summer to figure out how to stop McDavid, and the answer is still a shrug and a goalie change.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Thursday, October 1

Game recap

PIT7PHI0Final: PIT 7, PHI 0

The Flyers had all summer to plan their home opener and still forgot to show up for it. Pittsburgh, a team that's supposedly too old to climb stairs, led 5-0 halfway through the second and kept going. Nick Robertson scored twice, once shorthanded, because even down a man the Pens looked like they had the extra skater. Filip Hallander turned a promotion to the third line into three points. Evgeni Malkin, 40, scored on the power play like it was 2009. Arturs Silovs needed 19 saves for the shutout, which is barely a warmup. Dan Vladar saw 38 shots and seven goals, and that's less on him than on the five guys in front of him who spent the night sightseeing. Philly's last Cup was 1975, and on this evidence nobody in orange is in a hurry to update the banner.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI1TOR2Final: NYI 1, TOR 2

The Leafs won a hockey game, which in Toronto is basically a parade-route announcement. Two first-period goals from the bottom of the lineup, Colton Sissons and Easton Cowan, then 40 minutes of everyone in blue clutching the lead like a coupon. Auston Matthews and William Nylander combined for zero points and two shots, and somehow that's the formula. Anthony Stolarz stopped 26 of 27 on the back half of a back-to-back. The Islanders' only goal came from Emil Heineman while they were a man down, so maybe try that more often. Pete DeBoer's first night on the Island: 27 shots, one goal, and Matthew Schaefer playing 27:45 because apparently nobody else was cleared to. Long Island waited all summer for its team, and the offense is still stuck in traffic on the LIE.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK4COL8Final: LAK 4, COL 8

The Kings found out the hard way that killing penalties isn't optional in Denver. Colorado scored four times on the power play, and LA, in a twist nobody asked for, scored twice while shorthanded, so at least somebody on the Kings enjoyed special teams. Nathan MacKinnon scored twice and still found time to fight Brandt Clarke, a full shift's work in one night. Artturi Lehkonen added two power-play goals, Brock Nelson had three points, and Jared Bednar got a contract extension the same day and celebrated with eight goals. Darcy Kuemper stopped 21 of 29, a save percentage you usually find on a beer-league stat sheet. Artemi Panarin pulled LA within two with the net empty, and Colorado answered twice in 3:15. Life after Kopitar starts with eight goals against and a long flight home to think about it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Wednesday, September 30

Game recap

FLA1CAR0Final: FLA 1, CAR 0

The defending champs opened their title defense with 15 shots in 65 minutes, which is a very Hurricanes way to play: all forecheck, no evidence. Markstrom barely broke a sweat in his first game as a Panther, and the winner came from a defenseman in overtime, of course the first goal of the season between these two took 64 minutes and 55 seconds. Imama and Deslauriers handled the entertainment portion of the evening in the first period. The rest of it played like a tax audit with better lighting.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL3TOR2Final: MTL 3, TOR 2

Nylander scored before most of Scotiabank Arena found its seats, and for about ten minutes the new-look Leafs looked like a whole new team. Then the Canadiens scored three in a row and it looked like the old one. Alexandre Carrier, a defenseman, scored the unassisted winner, Josh Anderson did Josh Anderson things, and Toronto's late push got them within one and no closer. Marchenko's visa arrived just in time for him to find out what October in Toronto feels like. The good news for the Leafs: they get to try again tonight.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR0BOS3Final: NYR 0, BOS 3

For 56 minutes this was a goalie duel. For the last four it was a Bruins highlight reel: Minten, Peterka, then Kastelic into the empty net, three goals in 75 seconds of game time. Swayman pitched a 24-save shutout, and the Rangers' new-look forward group left with a clean sheet of zeroes in the points column. Dorofeyev fired five shots in his debut, which is five more than the Rangers got past Swayman. Shesterkin got zero help,

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN6EDM5Final: VAN 6, EDM 5

Last season's last-place team walked into Edmonton, went up 5-2, gave all of it back, and won anyway. Hockey is a beautiful, stupid sport. Evan Bouchard put up five points, a hat trick included, and still lost, which is about as cruel as opening night gets, besides letting three in the last two. Paul Cotter scored shorthanded to open it and in overtime to end it, bookending the chaos. Jarry got put on skates letting 6 of 23 go in. Same old story, the oily Edmonton net minders continue to be leaking worse than the Oiler's cup hopes in June.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI2VGK5Final: CHI 2, VGK 5

Patrick Kane scored in his first game back in a Blackhawks sweater, the United Center crowd would have loved it, except this was in Las Vegas. Thirty-nine seconds later Noah Hanifin restored the two-goal cushion, which is the kind of hospitality Vegas is famous for. Eichel ran the show with three points and the Knights outshot Chicago 36-26 under their new coach. The Hawks hung around for two periods, and hanging around is progress for a team that finished with 72 points last season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

NSH 4–5 TOR OT

Nashville Predators25 shots
4
Final/OTScotiabank Arena
5
Toronto Maple Leafs37 shots

Puckline's Report

Nashville built a 3-0 lead in Toronto and then handed it back one goal at a time, like a gambler who doesn't know when to leave the table. Steven Stamkos scored on the power play, Nils Hoglander scored twice, and it was 3-0 just 3:03 into the second. Then the Leafs woke up: John Tavares (with an assist from Anthony Stolarz, of all people), William Nylander on the power play, and after Stamkos made it 4-2, Gavin McKenna scored his first NHL goal. Jack Roslovic tied it 8:54 into the third, and Auston Matthews ended it 4:46 into overtime from Nylander, finishing with a goal and three assists. Toronto outshot Nashville 37-25. Juuse Saros made 32 saves; Stolarz made 21. The Leafs are 2-2. Nashville, 1-1-1, led by three on the road and left with one point, which is the most Predators way to spend a Tuesday.

Carolina Hurricanes34 shots
6
FinalCentre Bell
4
Montreal Canadiens20 shots

Puckline's Report

Montreal threw a home-opener party and the team that ended its season last spring showed up uninvited and ate all the food. The first period had five goals and no defense: Taylor Hall scored 2:25 in, Zachary Bolduc and Nick Suzuki answered inside two minutes, and Bolduc's power-play goal made it 3-2 Habs after one. Then Carolina took over. Sebastian Aho tied it on the power play, Mark Jankowski put the Canes ahead, and Hall's second made it 5-3 with eight minutes left. Juraj Slafkovsky got one back with the goalie pulled, and Andrei Svechnikov hit the empty net. Aho finished with a goal and two assists. Brandon Bussi, a surprise starter, won with 16 saves on 20; Jakub Dobes stopped 28 of 33. Carolina outshot Montreal 34-20. The Canadiens are 1-1-1 and have now allowed 12 goals in two games, which is a lot of pucks for one Bell Centre to watch go in.

OTT 3–5 DET

Ottawa Senators25 shots
3
FinalLittle Caesars Arena
5
Detroit Red Wings36 shots

Puckline's Report

Dylan Larkin asked to be traded this summer, lost the C, got booed at the opener, and then walked into his season debut and gave Detroit its first win. Hockey is a funny business. Tim Stützle opened it 2:44 in, Alex DeBrincat tied it 32 seconds later, and Larkin put the Wings ahead late in the first. Viktor Arvidsson scored on the power play and Justin Faulk made it 4-1 by 4:30 of the second. Drake Batherson and William Eklund pulled Ottawa within one, but DeBrincat finished it with a power-play empty-netter at 19:10 for his second of the night. Lucas Raymond had three assists, Larkin a goal and an assist, and rookie William Wallinder picked up a point in his NHL debut. John Gibson made 22 saves; Samuel Ersson made 31 on 35. Detroit is 1-2. Ottawa's perfect start lasted exactly two games, which is about one more than Senators fans had budgeted for.

Puckline's Report

Utah scored twice on the power play, and the Devils' defense went missing for the rest of it. Clayton Keller scored on the power play 1:57 in, Luke Evangelista answered on New Jersey's, and the teams traded goals until Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal (his fifth already) and Lawson Crouse's at 19:03 of the second made it 4-2. Jesper Boqvist got the Devils within one in the third, and Vincent Trocheck, playing through a lower-body injury, scored his first goal as a Mammoth to close it. Schmaltz had a goal and two assists, Mikhail Sergachev three assists. Evangelista scored both New Jersey goals, and Timo Meier fired eight shots for one assist. Brenden Dillon and Jack McBain fought in the third. Karel Vejmelka made 30 saves; Jake Allen stopped 26 of 31. Utah is 3-1. The Devils are 1-2 and minus-7, and the blue line is starting to look like a waiting room.

MIN 2–3 BUF OT

Minnesota Wild20 shots
2
Final/OTKeyBank Center
3
Buffalo Sabres28 shots

Puckline's Report

Minnesota led 2-0 with 25 minutes left and then remembered it was in Buffalo, where nice leads go to die. Danila Yurov scored on the power play at 13:53 of the second and Maxim Shabanov added another 1:45 later. Noah Ostlund cut it in half early in the third, Tage Thompson tied it at 9:38 on a night he reached 400 points as a Sabre, and Owen Power won it 4:22 into overtime from Jiri Kulich and Thompson. Thompson fired nine shots, Power and Thompson each had a goal and an assist, and Colten Ellis won his first start with 18 saves on 20. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 25 of 28. Matt Boldy had seven shots and nothing to show for them, and Kirill Kaprizov went pointless in 25 minutes. The Sabres are 2-1. The Wild got a point, which is nice, but they also blew a two-goal third-period lead to Buffalo, which is the kind of thing a team should keep out of the group chat.

Puckline's Report

Alexis Lafrenière got a hat trick, and two-thirds of it was delivered to an empty net 32 seconds apart. Nobody at MSG asked for a receipt. Oliver Bjorkstrand opened the scoring and Lafrenière made it 2-0 25 seconds into the second, but the Islanders tied it within five minutes on goals from Bo Horvat (power play) and Calum Ritchie. Bjorkstrand's power-play goal at 17:07 of the second was the winner, his second of the night and his first two as a Ranger. Lafrenière then scored at 18:22 and 18:54 of the third with Semyon Varlamov on the bench. He also had an assist. There were two fights: Brayden Schenn and J.T. Miller in the first, Bjorkstrand and Adam Pelech in the final seconds. Varlamov, in his first NHL game since November 2024, made 19 saves; Igor Shesterkin made 17. The Rangers have won four straight. The Islanders are 1-2 and lost the Battle of New York on a pair of empty nets.

STL 2–4 CHI

St Louis Blues28 shots
2
FinalUnited Center
4
Chicago Blackhawks21 shots

Puckline's Report

Chicago finally won a hockey game, and it picked the home opener to do it, which is good showmanship from a team that hadn't shown much else. Mason McTavish gave St. Louis the lead late in the first. In the second, Sam Rinzel tied it on the power play and Anton Frondell put the Hawks ahead two minutes later. The last 69 seconds were a fire drill: Cole Smith scored shorthanded into the empty net, Connor McMichael answered on the power play with Hofer pulled, and Frank Nazar hit the empty net again with four seconds left. Nazar and Frondell each had a goal and an assist. Spencer Knight made 26 saves on 28; Joel Hofer stopped 17 of 19. Colton Parayko tied Barret Jackman for the most games by a Blues defenseman. St. Louis is 1-2 to close its opening road trip and just gave a 1-3 rebuild its first win of the year. That's charity, not hockey.

VGK 6–2 SEA

Vegas Golden Knights28 shots
6
FinalClimate Pledge Arena
2
Seattle Kraken27 shots

Puckline's Report

Vegas went to Seattle and treated the Kraken like a comp'd buffet. It was 5-0 before the second intermission: Victor Olofsson scored twice, Tomas Hertl on the power play, Mark Stone shorthanded, and Jack Eichel unassisted with 31 seconds left in the period. Hertl added another power-play goal in the third. Hertl (two goals, two assists) and Eichel (a goal, three assists) had four points each. Joey Daccord was pulled after allowing five on 21 shots; Philipp Grubauer stopped 6 of 7. Shane Wright and Jared McCann scored for Seattle. It got nasty late: Brandon Montour fought Stone and took 17 penalty minutes, Marc Gatcomb fought Ryan Winterton, and Ben Meyers was thrown out for boarding Olofsson, with a league hearing expected. Carter Hart made 25 saves. Vegas is 3-1. Seattle is 2-2, and the Kraken's best work of the night came after the game was already gone.

Florida Panthers28 shots
2
FinalCrypto.com Arena
1
Los Angeles Kings20 shots

Puckline's Report

The Panthers needed four games and a cross-country flight to win one in regulation, but they got it, 2-1 in the Kings' home opener. Alex Laferriere scored with a minute left in the first for Los Angeles. Seth Jones tied it 3:49 into the second, and Matthew Tkachuk won it at 11:20 of the third from Sam Bennett. Jacob Markstrom stopped 19 of 20, and the Kings managed just 20 shots in their own building. Darcy Kuemper made 26 saves on 28 and deserved better. Garnet Hathaway and Joel Edmundson fought in the second. Artemi Panarin had four shots and no points. Florida is 2-0-2. Los Angeles is 0-2-1, one of two teams in the West still without a win, and its home crowd paid opening-night prices to watch 20 shots in 60 minutes.

PIT @ WSH · 7:30 PM ET

Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT2-1-0 · 4 PTS
@7:30 PM ETWed Oct 7 · Capital One Arena
PIT +134MLWSH -162
Washington CapitalsWSH1-1-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline Preview

Two days after Alex Ovechkin announced this will be his last NHL season, Washington opens its building and the farewell tour gets its first home date. Naturally, Sidney Crosby is the opening act. Counting the playoffs, tonight is their 101st meeting: Crosby has 97 points head-to-head, Ovechkin 71, and Pittsburgh won three of their four playoff series (2009 and 2017; Washington got 2018). The Capitals took last season's series 2-1, finishing with Logan Thompson's 3-0 shutout on Apr. 12, a night billed as maybe Ovi's last home game. It wasn't, and Washington missed the playoffs anyway.

Ovechkin has one assist in two games, and Spencer Carbery has put him with Dylan Strome and Anthony Beauvillier. Matt Roy is doubtful, with Dylan McIlrath next in. Pittsburgh is 2-1 with 15 goals, seven of them in Philadelphia, but it blew a 2-0 lead at home to Winnipeg on Monday. Crosby has two assists and no goals, and Evgeni Malkin, on a one-year deal, has four points. Bryan Rust could make his season debut if the Penguins clear a roster spot. Arturs Silovs and Thompson are projected. Washington has also averaged 20.5 penalty minutes a game, which is a strange way to spend a farewell tour: watching the penalty kill from the bench.

By Puckline Prince

COL @ WPG · 7:30 PM ET

Colorado AvalancheCOL2-0-0 · 4 PTS
@7:30 PM ETWed Oct 7 · Canada Life Centre
COL -196MLWPG +162
Winnipeg JetsWPG2-0-1 · 5 PTS

Puckline Preview

The last two Presidents' Trophy winners meet in Winnipeg, and only one of them still looks the part. Colorado is 2-0 with 14 goals in two home games: 8-4 over Los Angeles, the most the franchise has ever scored in an opener, and 6-1 over St. Louis. Nathan MacKinnon has five points and Artturi Lehkonen three goals. Jared Bednar still called the rush coverage in the opener 'rough,' which is coach for 'four goals against the Kings is too many.' This is the front end of a back-to-back, with Calgary tomorrow, and Mackenzie Blackwood is projected.

Winnipeg is 2-0-1 on a goalie budget. Connor Hellebuyck asked out, didn't report and is suspended, and Pierre LeBrun says he won't accept a trade to any Canadian team. Stuart Skinner is projected after Clay Stevenson won his debut in Pittsburgh. Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti have five points each, Perfetti has two game-winners, and the power play is 4-for-8. Scott Arniel is in the last year of his contract after the Jets went from 116 points to 35-35-12 and no playoffs. Colorado won last season's series 2-1, but Winnipeg took the last meeting, 4-2 in Denver on Mar. 28, on a late Perfetti tip. In the playoffs it's all Avalanche: they took the 2024 first round in five after losing Game 1 7-6. Eighteen months ago the Jets had the best record in hockey. Now their best goalie is spending the season deciding which provinces he doesn't like.

By Puckline Prince

EDM @ ANA · 10:00 PM ET

Edmonton OilersEDM2-0-1 · 5 PTS
@10:00 PM ETWed Oct 7 · Honda Center
EDM -134MLANA +112
Anaheim DucksANA2-0-0 · 4 PTS

Puckline Preview

The last time these two met, Anaheim was ending Edmonton's season. The Ducks won last spring's first round in six, their first series win since 2017. Game 4 went to overtime and was decided by a Ryan Poehling goal that went in off Darnell Nurse's skate, waved off at first and allowed after a long review. Game 6 was a 5-2 clincher at Honda Center on Apr. 30. The Oilers, two-time defending West champions at the time, came out of it with a new coach, Mike Babcock, whose hiring drew loud criticism.

Edmonton is 2-0-1 and plays like a pinball machine: 5.67 goals a game, Connor McDavid with nine points (five of them in a 9-7 win in Vancouver), Evan Bouchard with eight. It also allows 4.67 a game, 29th, with a 57.1% penalty kill, dead last. Frederik Andersen is on LTIR, possibly until December, and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is out, and Mike Babcock has named Devon Levi (.810) the starter. Anaheim is 2-0, both by one goal, despite being outshot in both; Lukas Dostal is projected after stopping 56 of 61. Leo Carlsson leads with five points, Troy Terry is out after hip surgery, and the Ducks are reported to be recalling Roger McQueen and defenseman Stian Solberg. Edmonton's whole plan is to outscore its own goaltending, which worked great right up until last April.

By Puckline Prince
